title: Wedge sampling of pars petrosa for ancient DNA extraction
author: Raphaela Stahl

steps.title: Prepare Workstation and Materials
steps.instruction: Set up a clean workspace to avoid cross-contamination, ensuring all materials that contact the sample are decontaminated.

substeps.instruction: Place a sheet of aluminium foil under the hood.
Place weighing paper, drill bits, and tooth pliers/forceps on a second sheet of aluminium foil on a clean surface outside the hood (or inside the hood, covered with foil or paper towels).

Gather necessary supplies: 2 ml Safe-Lock Biopure tubes, weighing trays/pans, labelled sample bags, small aluminium foil pieces, tape strips, paper towels, 1:10 diluted commercial bleach solution, and UV-irradiated filtered/deionised water.

steps.title: UV-Irradiate the Bone
steps.instruction: Decontaminate the pars petrosa using UV radiation.

substeps.instruction: Place a sheet of aluminium foil in the UV chamber.
Place the pars petrosa on the foil and place the corresponding labelled sample bag next to it.
UV-irradiate the bone for 00:15:00 on each side.
Use precision forceps to handle bones individually to avoid direct contact.

steps.title: Prepare Sample Tube and Scale
steps.instruction: Prepare the collection tube and calibrate the scale.

substeps.instruction: Label a new 2 ml tube with the sample ID on the lid and the side.
Place the tube in the center of the precision scale and tare it.
Label a new sample bag with the sample ID for use after sampling.
Keep tubes closed until bone powder is added, opening them only inside the hood.

steps.title: Prepare Weighing Paper
steps.instruction: Prepare the surface for powder collection.

substeps.instruction: Using a new pair of gloves, take a weighing tray.
Crease a sheet of weighing paper mid-way and place it under the sampling area to facilitate powder transfer.

steps.title: Perform Wedge Cut of Pars Petrosa
steps.instruction: Expose the densest part of the bone around the cochlea using a wedge cut.

substeps.instruction: Hold the bone fraction with a tooth plier at the temporal bone.
Using a round diamond saw blade, cut from the apex partis petrosae, following the margo superior partis petrosae, and stop shortly after the internal acoustic opening (meatus acusticus internus).
Target area 'c' (located roughly halfway between the jugular fossa and the petrous crest) for optimal aDNA yield.

steps.title: Protect Bone Surface
steps.instruction: Prevent surface contaminants from mixing with the drilled powder.

substeps.instruction: Wrap the sample with aluminium foil and/or tape, leaving only the specific area to be drilled unwrapped.

steps.title: Drill and Collect Bone Powder
steps.instruction: Extract bone powder from the cochlear region.

substeps.instruction: Drill at low speed and high torque within the cochlear region, parallel to the auditory canal.
Collect clean bone powder on the weighing paper.
Carefully tip the drilling hole to empty it onto the collection paper.
If dirt/soil is mixed with powder, separate them by repeatedly tipping the edges of the weighing paper to utilize differences in weight and particle size; discard the dirt.

steps.title: Transfer and Weigh Powder
steps.instruction: Collect the powder into the tube and record the mass.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the clean bone powder into the labelled 2 ml Safe-Lock Biopure tube using the folded weighing paper.
Close the tube, wipe it with a damp paper towel, and weigh it on the previously tared scale.
If powder is statically charged, apply an anti-static gun to the weighing paper and tube.
Aim for 30 mg to 50 mg of powder; if more than 50 mg is collected, store the excess as back-up in a separate tube.
Note the weight in mg on the side of the tube (not on the lid).
Store the bone powder at -20 °C.

steps.title: Post-Sampling Documentation and Storage
steps.instruction: Document the process and store the remaining bone.

substeps.instruction: Take photos of the sample for documentation.
Place the bone back into a new, UV-irradiated, labelled bag.

steps.title: Decontaminate Workstation and Tools
steps.instruction: Clean all equipment to prevent cross-contamination between samples.

substeps.instruction: Discard disposable materials (aluminium foil, weighing trays/pans).
Clean surfaces and pliers with 1:10 bleach solution, then wipe with water-wet paper towels and air dry.
Clean sensitive electronic devices (drill handpiece, precision balance) with less aggressive reagents like DNA away.
Clean reusable drill bits and saw blades by incubating them in 1:10 bleach solution for at least 2 minutes.
Brush saw blades with a UV-irradiated and bleached toothbrush, then clean with UV-irradiated water and dry.
Replace drill bits after approximately 5 uses.
